notes:
Default is untouched: DecideOptions.reveal defaults to Reveal::Default and sample_world() calls determinize_with exactly as before in that case (same rng draws). Unit test (a) checks sample_world(Default) == determinize_with on 8 seeds and decide output identical; goldens (audit 3,386 + replay 200) pass; the default latency run reproduced the previous WP's 20 games move for move (2,512 moves, identical count).
Visibility table (hidden_zones_table) follows the OPCG zone rules: deck = non-public to both players (owner included); hand = public to owner only; life = face-down cards are non-public to both players incl. the owner, face-up life is public; field/stage/leader/trash/cost area (DON!!) are public. In the engine the only per-card visibility flag is CardInstance.is_face_up (used for life); the engine does not track 'revealed' hand cards or known deck positions (e.g. after a look-and-put-to-bottom effect), so fair treats them as hidden. That is a conservative simplification: fair slightly over-hides vs. a real player's knowledge.
temp_zone is left untouched in all modes: it holds cards an effect is currently looking at (own look effects -> visible to me). An opponent's temp_zone during my decision would be hidden in real play but is transient and rare; not shuffled (noted, not handled).
Interpretation choice for opp_hand: the spec says 'shuffle only the opp deck (and the face-down areas mixed into it)'. I shuffle the opp deck ONLY and keep opp face-down life real, because the current determinization and omniscient both keep opp life real; this makes the decomposition clean: default -> opp_hand differs only in knowing the opp hand; opp_hand -> omniscient differs only in the opp deck order. If the coordinator wanted opp life shuffled too in opp_hand, it is a one-line change (hidden_slots(..., life=true)).
fair pools: opponent pool = opp hand + opp deck + opp face-down life, drawn with one shuffle_order call; own pool = own deck + own face-down life, a second call (opp first). Per-zone counts preserved; face-up life cards keep their positions; empty pools draw nothing from the rng.
omniscient + reveal together -> EngineError::BadPayload from DecideOptions::validate (called in decide() and in decide_opts_and_carry). An unknown reveal string or a non-string value is also an error at the JSON layer (not silently defaulted), because a typo would otherwise silently measure the default.
reveal keeps worlds>1 working (unlike omniscient): each world i re-samples with its own rng as before.
TreeMcts::run in mcts.rs still calls determinize_with directly; not on the decide path (same as the previous WP), left alone.
Local arenas (40 pairs each, ~+-55 Elo CI) are indicative only: opp_hand +43.7 [0.45..0.67], fair -34.9 [0.33..0.57], vs. omniscient +79.5 local (+83.7 production). Read naively: knowing the opp hand gives roughly half of the omniscient gain, and fair (not seeing own future draws/life) is worse than the current shipped search, i.e. the current search's gain may partly come from peeking at its own deck order. Too wide to decide; the production arenas (§7.25) are the judge.
Latency: per-move mean on one core is about the same for all three (default 0.153 s, opp_hand 0.166, fair 0.148); games length differs (moves over 20 games: 2512 / 2672 / 2853).
The container restarted once during the opp_hand arena (uptime reset); arena_shard resumed from its jsonl ledger, 40 distinct seeds, no duplicates.
Container lacked maturin/pytest/fastapi; installed via pip (maturin, opcg_sim/requirements.txt, pytest, pytest-xdist) before the gate.
